robot: two ARX X5 6-joint arms with parallel two-finger grippers at a table (RoboDojo's dual-arm setup)

frame.suite: RoboDojo's scene frame: x to the right seen from behind the arms, y forward from the arm bases, z up
frame.base_text: the robot base frame: midway between the two arm bases on the table top (z = table top), +X forward towards the far side of the table, +Y towards the left arm, +Z up; the left arm's base is at (0, +0.3, 0) and the right arm's at (0, -0.3, 0)

left.note: 6 joints (joint1..6, rad); end-effector pose = the arm's link6 frame; gripper command 1 = open .. 0 = closed in RoboDojo's own scale

ee.point: the arm's link6 frame (the last wrist link; the fingers reach beyond it)
ee.mode_text: the service solves each pose with the arm's kinematic model and runs it as a joint move at most 0.25 m/s (duration_s does not apply); a miss of more than 1 cm is reported

right.note: 6 joints (joint1..6, rad); end-effector pose = the arm's link6 frame; gripper command 1 = open .. 0 = closed in RoboDojo's own scale

ee.point: the arm's link6 frame (the last wrist link; the fingers reach beyond it)
ee.mode_text: the service solves each pose with the arm's kinematic model and runs it as a joint move at most 0.25 m/s (duration_s does not apply); a miss of more than 1 cm is reported

notes: Every 25 Hz action counts against the task's step limit (results give steps_left): a joint row dt = k x 0.04 s uses k steps, an end-effector goal uses as many steps as its move takes at 0.25 m/s, and observe or wait with seconds > 0 uses seconds x 25 steps; observe without seconds uses none. Plan short, direct moves and pass duration_s to joint moves when time matters. The gripper value in the state is the command in force; the measured opening (0..1, 1 = fully open; a gripper closed on an object stops above 0) is in proprio_now (left_gripper_opening, right_gripper_opening). Joint efforts (left_joint1_effort ...) grow when an arm pushes on something. A joint goal for one arm also re-sends the other arm's measured joints.
